record.title: COMED selectively escalates cross-model collaboration to trade rescue gains against collaboration harms
record.summary: The Sep. 22, 2026 COMED paper studies when a multi-model system should trust its initial answer, check it with a peer, or invoke fuller collaboration. The controller uses anchor self-consistency, router ambiguity and a lightweight peer probe to direct additional model calls toward uncertain or persistently disagreeing cases. In its reported benchmark suite, COMED improves its fixed or routed anchor in all 16 open-weight settings, averaging 4.6 percentage points while using at most two distinct models per query and about 33% fewer decoded tokens than dense collaboration. A Frontier-3/Humanity's Last Exam stress test reports GPT-5.5 rising from 23.13% to 28.13%, with collaboration on 70% of examples. These are paper-reported results; independent reproduction and implementation evidence remain open.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: The authors published COMED, a post-anchor controller that chooses to accept an anchor answer, verify it with a peer, or escalate to cross-model collaboration.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: Across 16 open-weight settings spanning medical, scientific and general reasoning benchmarks, the paper reports that COMED improves its corresponding fixed or routed anchor in every setting, averaging +4.6 percentage points, with at most two models per query and about 33% fewer decoded tokens than dense collaboration.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: In a Frontier-3/Humanity's Last Exam stress test, the paper reports GPT-5.5 accuracy increasing from 23.13% to 28.13%, with collaboration used on 70% of examples.

claims.label: NOT_ESTABLISHED
claims.text: The reported results are author-run benchmark results in specified model pools and evaluation settings; this review found no independent reproduction or public code artifact and they do not establish general deployment gains.

evidence_gaps.description: Independent reproduction of the main 16 open-weight settings and the Frontier-3/HLE result with pinned model versions, splits, decoding budgets and scoring.
Measure actual latency, throughput, monetary cost and hardware utilization rather than decoded-token and model-call proxies.
Test controller calibration and rescue-harm behavior under prompt, task-distribution and model-pool shifts.

brief.importance_rationale: If the paper-reported gains hold under independent matched evaluation, a harm-aware controller for selective multi-model collaboration could improve accuracy while reducing inference cost across several model pools. The scope is meaningful for inference design but remains benchmark-bound and unreplicated.
limitations: All performance results are author-reported; no independent reproduction was found in this review.
The evaluation uses specific benchmark datasets, model pools and thresholds; it does not establish generalization to production traffic, other providers, or different tasks.
Decoded tokens and model-call counts are proxies for inference cost; latency, monetary cost, throughput and serving hardware effects are not established.
The Frontier-3/HLE experiment is a bounded stress test and does not establish broad frontier-model gains.
The controller depends on sampled self-consistency and a learned router; sensitivity to distribution shift, prompt changes and calibration error remains relevant.
brief.summary: The Sep. 22, 2026 COMED paper studies when a multi-model system should trust its initial answer, check it with a peer, or invoke fuller collaboration. The controller uses anchor self-consistency, router ambiguity and a lightweight peer probe to direct additional model calls toward uncertain or persistently disagreeing cases. In its reported benchmark suite, COMED improves its fixed or routed anchor in all 16 open-weight settings, averaging 4.6 percentage points while using at most two distinct models per query and about 33% fewer decoded tokens than dense collaboration. A Frontier-3/Humanity's Last Exam stress test reports GPT-5.5 rising from 23.13% to 28.13%, with collaboration on 70% of examples. These are paper-reported results; independent reproduction and implementation evidence remain open.

technical.claimed_result: The authors report gains over the corresponding fixed or routed anchor across all 16 open-weight settings (mean +4.6 percentage points), at most two distinct models per query and approximately 33% fewer decoded tokens than dense always-on collaboration. In a Frontier-3/HLE stress test, GPT-5.5 is reported at 23.13% without COMED and 28.13% with it; COMED collaborates on 70% of examples.
technical.compute_or_cost: The paper reports decoded-token counts and distinct model calls, including about 33% fewer decoded tokens than dense collaboration for the main sparse Top-1 controller. It does not establish real serving latency, monetary cost, throughput, or hardware-level savings.
technical.demonstrated_result: The arXiv v1 paper, its controller pseudocode, benchmark tables and stated experimental configuration are directly inspectable. The performance numbers are author-reported experimental claims and have not been independently reproduced in this review.
technical.implementation_status: Research prototype evaluated offline on benchmarks; no production deployment is reported.
technical.mechanism: After an anchor model answers, COMED uses sampled-answer self-consistency and a router margin to accept high-confidence cases, probes a top-ranked peer for ambiguous cases, and escalates only when disagreement persists with high confidence. It formalizes the tradeoff as rescued anchor errors minus collaboration-induced harms.
technical.novelty: Combines post-anchor selective escalation with a rescue-harm framing, distinguishing answer routing from whether to trust an already-produced answer and whether peer collaboration is worth its cost and risk.
technical.regime: Open-weight experiments use pools of three or four models, medical/scientific/general reasoning benchmark families, fixed-anchor and learned-router regimes, and a default Top-1 collaboration budget. The Frontier-3 test uses a GPT-5.5 anchor on Humanity's Last Exam. Reported results are limited to these model and benchmark settings.
technical.reproducibility: The paper specifies model pools, dataset splits, router training and controller hyperparameters in its appendices. No public implementation or independent reproduction was recovered during this review; authors' reported results remain credible but unconfirmed.
technical.strongest_baseline: Corresponding fixed-anchor or learned-router systems without post-anchor control, plus dense Always-Collaborate and majority-vote baselines under the paper's evaluation protocol.

brief.title: COMED selectively escalates cross-model collaboration to trade rescue gains against collaboration harms
brief.why_it_matters: The work makes cross-model collaboration a selective inference-time decision and explicitly accounts for peers correcting wrong answers as well as corrupting correct ones. If independently reproduced, the controller could improve accuracy-cost tradeoffs in multi-model serving. The current evidence is bounded to author-run benchmarks and does not establish production impact.
